claims.text: Adding approximately 1–3 vol.% nanoscale Y2O3 particles to MoNbTaVW will increase its yield strength.
Adding approximately 1–3 vol.% nanoscale Y2O3 particles to MoNbTaVW will enhance its creep resistance.
The proposed mechanical improvements will persist at 1000–1200°C and under irradiation.
The Y2O3 addition will not compromise the thermal or irradiation stability of MoNbTaVW.
Mechanical alloying followed by consolidation can introduce Y2O3 nanoparticles into the MoNbTaVW matrix.
Advanced dispersion techniques and in-situ process monitoring will produce a uniform Y2O3 distribution and preserve nanoparticle stability during processing.
The intervention will create uniformly dispersed nanoscale Y2O3 precipitates in the alloy matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will remain stable during service at 1000–1200°C and under irradiation.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will hinder dislocation motion through dispersion strengthening.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as sinks for irradiation-induced point defects and dislocation loops.
Defect-sink activity will delay irradiation-defect accumulation and stabilize the microstructure.
The Y2O3 dispersion will not degrade the phase stability of MoNbTaVW.
The modified alloy is predicted to have a 15–20% higher yield strength than nanoparticle-free MoNbTaVW.
Uniform nanoparticle dispersion is necessary for the predicted mechanical improvement.
Nanoparticle agglomeration or processing inhomogeneity may compromise the predicted improvement.
The magnitude of the mechanical improvement may depend on irradiation dose and temperature.
